name: Ivan Kramskoi
bio: Ivan Nikolayevich Kramskoi was a Russian Realist painter and art critic. One of the most prominent artisans during Tsar Alexander II's reign, he is remembered as co-founding member and public frontman of the Peredvizhniki movement.

paintings.title: Portrait of an Unknown Woman
paintings.story: Portrait of an Unknown Woman, also known as The Unknown Woman, An Unknown Lady or Stranger is an oil painting by the Russian artist Ivan Kramskoi, painted in 1883. The model, whose identity is unknown, is a woman of "quiet strength and forthright gaze". It is one of Russia's best-known artworks, although a number of critics were indignant when the painting was first exhibited and condemned what they saw as a depiction of a haughty and immoral woman. Its popularity has grown with changes in public taste.
facts: Portrait of an Unknown Woman combines elements of the genre and portrait traditions in art.
She is dressed in a black fur and velvet coat, fur hat, with leather gloves.

paintings.title: Christ in the Desert
paintings.story: Christ in the Desert or Christ in the Wilderness is an 1872 painting by Russian artist Ivan Kramskoi, reflecting the temptation of Christ. Kramskoi was offered a professorship for the painting by the Russian Academy of Arts Council but rejected it in the beginning of 1873. He had been expelled from the Academy earlier, and chose to keep his "youthful commitment to independence from the Academy". Subsequently, it became one of the favourite paintings of Pavel Tretyakov, who bought it for his gallery in the year the painting was finished.
facts: The thoughtful figure of Christ, wearing a dark wrap and a red tunic underneath, is slightly shifted to the right of centre.
The theme of Christ's temptation had attracted Kramskoi already in the early 1860s.

paintings.title: The Mermaids (Kramskoi)
paintings.story: The Mermaids is an 1871 oil-on-canvas by the Russian artist Ivan Kramskoi.
facts: The painting is set at night and is almost entirely without colour.
The women occupy the centre mid-ground of the painting and are lit from high above the left hand of the canvas, presumably by the moon.

paintings.title: Self-Portrait (Kramskoi)
paintings.story: Self-Portrait is an oil-on-canvas painting of 1867 by the Russian artist Ivan Kramskoi. Oval in shape, it is a self-evaluation: Kramskoi indicates how he sees his own facial features and his relationship with the world around him. Then 30 years old, the artist renders himself formally dressed, handsome and intelligent-looking. His pose causes him to be gaze down on the viewer, with an appearance that is, according to the Tretyakov Gallery, "severe and demanding".
